title: Cuts From A Knife; Circumcise Me Is Amusing But Misses Opportunities

contact_edits.before: At the opposite extreme: The most visually and conceptually exciting theatre in Toronto has been happening, not for the first time, at the Canadian Opera Company. Its production of Gluck's Iphigenia in Tauris, in its compression and concentration, cut to the merciless heart of concentration and compression. Its Rigoletto was set in a plush 19thcentury men's club, brilliantly created by the great Canadian designer Michael Levine. The program notes claimed that this was a comment on the patriarchal society in which the story is set, but it was selling itself short; what we saw was a privileged group ganging up on all outsiders, including the crippled clowning protagonist; which is what the Verdi work is all about. (The singing in both productions was great, too, but you expect that.) ? Circumcise Me runs through Nov. 6 at the Jane Mallett Theatre. For showtimes and ticket information visit hgjewishtheatre.com or call 416-366-7723.
